weeks.title: The Anatomy of a Compelling Story

quiz.title: Module 3 — Tuesday — The Art of Effective Storytelling
quiz.description: Tuesday's quiz covers what makes a story memorable, the three ingredients of effective storytelling, the five senses framework, reporting against reliving, the present-tense technique, why sharing meaning matters, when storytelling suits a situation, and the closing message about authoring your own story.

questions.prompt: According to the video, what makes a story powerful and memorable?
options: Having extraordinary life experiences.
Using complicated vocabulary.
The perspective and meaning the storyteller brings to the experience.
Speaking loudly and confidently.
questions.explanation: The events are only the raw material. What makes a story land is the meaning the teller draws out of them — which is why an ordinary experience told well beats an extraordinary one told flatly.

questions.prompt: What are the three essential ingredients of effective storytelling discussed in the video?
options: Be specific, relive the story, and share its meaning.
Use humour, exaggerate events, and speak quickly.
Introduce characters, create suspense, and add statistics.
Use simple words, avoid emotions, and keep stories short.
questions.explanation: Specificity puts the listener in the scene, reliving makes them feel it, and the meaning tells them why it mattered. The three build on each other.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of using the five senses framework when telling a story?
options: To make the story longer and more complicated.
To help the storyteller remember every event in chronological order.
To replace emotions with physical descriptions.
To help the audience visualize and experience the events being described.
questions.explanation: Sensory detail gives the listener something to see, hear and feel. That is what turns a description into an experience they can share.

questions.prompt: What is the main difference between reporting a story and reliving a story?
options: Reporting uses emotions, while reliving uses only facts.
Reporting simply explains what happened, while reliving allows the audience to experience the moment through vivid details and emotions.
Reporting is always more persuasive than reliving.
Reliving a story means changing the original events.
questions.explanation: A report hands over facts; reliving puts the listener inside the moment. The events are the same — the difference is whether the audience feels them.

questions.prompt: According to the video, which technique helps a storyteller make an audience feel as though they are experiencing the event in real time?
options: Avoiding gestures while speaking.
Using only past-tense sentences.
Changing to the present tense and allowing body language to reflect the experience.
Focusing entirely on statistics.
questions.explanation: Present tense collapses the distance between the telling and the event, and matching body language reinforces it. The listener stops hearing about it and starts being in it.

questions.prompt: Why is sharing the meaning of a story important?
options: It helps the audience understand the lesson and how the story relates to their own lives.
It makes the story sound more complicated.
It allows the storyteller to avoid explaining the events.
It ensures that every story ends with humour.
questions.explanation: Without the meaning, the audience has to guess why they were told it. Naming the lesson lets them connect it to their own experience.

questions.prompt: According to the video, when is storytelling most appropriate?
options: Every time someone asks a simple yes-or-no question.
Only when speaking to large audiences.
Whenever the storyteller wants to entertain people.
When you have around 15 minutes or more and want to be memorable and influential.
questions.explanation: A story takes time to build. With a few minutes it crowds out the point; given real time, it is what people remember afterwards.

questions.prompt: What is the most important lesson from the video's closing message about storytelling?
options: Only professional writers can create meaningful stories.
You are the author of your own story, so live the experiences you want to tell.
Every life experience must become a public story.
Successful storytelling depends entirely on having an exciting life.
questions.explanation: The closing turns the craft back on the teller: the material comes from the life you choose to live, so the story starts before you open your mouth.
